facts.text: On this date in 1972, Palestinian militants seized Israeli athletes at the Munich Olympics — an event that prompted Israel to create what became the world's most-copied airport security model, now standard in 47 countries.
On Sept 5, 1905, the Treaty of Portsmouth ended the Russo-Japanese War — the first modern peace deal where an Asian power defeated a European one, reshaping every colonial calculation on earth.

Mongolia has more horses than people — roughly 4.3 million horses to 3.4 million humans — and a third of the population still lives nomadically, making it the least densely populated sovereign nation on earth.

The Philippines is the world's largest supplier of nurses, with more registered nurses working abroad than at home — a deliberate 1970s government policy that turned human emigration into the country's second-largest source of GDP.

Istanbul sits in two continents, but so does its subway: the Marmaray line crosses the Bosphorus underwater, making it one of the only metro systems on earth that physically connects Europe and Asia beneath an active sea.
On this day in 1929, economist Roger Babson publicly predicted an imminent stock market crash. Six weeks later, Black Thursday arrived and wiped out billions.
On Sept 5, 1975, Ford Motor Company went public — except it had already been public since 1956. The '75 offering was simply the Ford Foundation quietly cashing out $350M in shares.
The entire global derivatives market is estimated at over $1 quadrillion notional value — roughly 10x world GDP. Most of it will never be exercised; it exists as a vast web of hedges and bets.
When Volkswagen briefly became the world's most valuable company in October 2008, it was because a short squeeze forced its stock to $1,000. Porsche had quietly cornered 74% of shares.
The word 'salary' comes from the Latin 'salarium' — the ration of salt given to Roman soldiers. Salt was once scarce enough to constitute real wages.
On this date in 1977, Voyager 1 launched. It is now so far away that its radio signals, traveling at the speed of light, take over 22 hours to reach Earth.
On September 5, 1882, the first Labor Day was observed — but the human spine has its own calendar: it compresses up to 1cm by day's end and fully rebounds overnight.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons.
Your body replaces the lining of your small intestine every two to four days — one of the fastest cell turnover rates in any organ, driven by constant chemical bombardment from digestion.
Octopuses have three hearts, and two of them stop beating when the animal swims, which is why octopuses prefer crawling — swimming exhausts them.
On this day in 1977, Voyager 1 launched. It is now farther from Earth than any human-made object in history — and it still phones home, on power equivalent to a refrigerator light bulb.
On this day in 1972, Palestinian militants seized Israeli athletes at the Munich Olympics. The German police unit created in response, GSG 9, has never lost a hostage in a rescue operation.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford traces to 1096; Tenochtitlán was founded in 1325.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; the pyramid was finished around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone. Scotland's Alexander Bain sent images over wire while most of the world still traveled by horse.
Meraki (μεράκι): Greek for doing something with soul, creativity, and love — leaving a piece of yourself in your work. There is no single English equivalent, which says something about English.
Sonder: the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined in 2012 by John Koenig; too useful to remain obscure.

On this day in 1698, Peter the Great imposed a tax on beards, forcing Russian men to carry a copper token proving they had paid to keep their facial hair. The word for beard tax has no English name — an oversight.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or perhaps never had. Grief and longing folded into a single syllable cluster English simply cannot replicate.
On this day in 1774, the First Continental Congress convened — and the word 'congress' itself comes from Latin congressus, meaning a coming together, a meeting, a collision.

On this date in 2017, China's People's Bank declared ICOs illegal and ordered all raised funds returned — triggering a 40% drop in Bitcoin's price within days and accelerating the offshore exodus that built today's offshore crypto legal infrastructure.

On September 5, 2022, Ethereum completed its final dress rehearsal merge on the Goerli testnet, exactly one week before the Mainnet Merge — the moment proof-of-work Ethereum effectively ceased to exist.

Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet holds no coins — it holds cryptographic claims to unspent outputs. When you 'send' bitcoin, you destroy those outputs and mint new ones, much like breaking a banknote.

The DAO hack of 2016 drained 3.6 million ETH through a reentrancy bug, but the attacker was bound by the same 28-day withdrawal lock they exploited — giving the Ethereum community just enough time to hard fork.

Satoshi Nakamoto's 1 million estimated bitcoin have never moved. On-chain analysis identifies them by a distinctive nonce pattern called the 'Patoshi pattern', making them among the most-watched addresses in cryptographic history.

On this date in 2009, Rajat Raina and Andrew Ng published 'Large-scale Deep Unsupervised Learning using Graphics Processors' — one of the first papers to demonstrate GPUs could make neural nets practical at scale.
On this date in 2017, DeepMind's AlphaGo was officially retired after defeating Ke Jie 3-0. It never lost a game to a professional human player in formal competition.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of about 4,600 average US households.
The largest transformer models now have more parameters than the human brain has synapses. A human brain has roughly 100 trillion synapses; some sparse mixture-of-experts models exceed that count.
RLHF, the technique that made ChatGPT feel coherent, was first published in 2017 by OpenAI on a video game agent trained to play Atari — the human feedback component involved just 900 queries.
